questions.stem: Which of the following statements about elagolix is false?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a gonadotropin release hormone antagonist

options.label: C
options.text: It is approved for treatment of pain due to endometriosis

options.label: D
options.text: It can cause hot flashes as adverse effect

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) It is not effective orally

 

  • Elagolix is an orally active gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist. 
  • It is effective when taken by mouth, which makes it a convenient option for patients. 
  • This statement is false because elagolix is indeed effective when administered orally.

 

Other Options: 

 

Option A. It is a gonadotropin release hormone antagonist: This statement is true. Elagolix works as a GnRH antagonist, which means it inhibits the action of GnRH and reduces the production of gonadotropins (LH and FSH).

 

Option C. It is approved for treatment of pain due to endometriosis: This statement is true. Elagolix has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis.

 

Option D. It can cause hot flashes as adverse effect: This statement is true. One of the known adverse effects of elagolix is the occurrence of hot flashes, which is related to its mechanism of reducing estrogen levels in the body.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Elagolix is an orally active gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist approved for the treatment of moderate to severe pain associated with endometriosis. 
  • It effectively reduces the production of gonadotropins and estrogen, which can alleviate endometriosis-related pain. 
  • However, its estrogen-lowering effect can lead to side effects such as hot flashes. 
  • Understanding the pharmacokinetics, therapeutic indications, and potential adverse effects of elagolix is crucial for its appropriate use in clinical practice.

questions.stem: A young married couple has been trying to have a child for four years, but without success despite not using any contraceptives. The husband's sperm count is within the normal range. The doctor advised the wife to undergo treatment to enhance fertility. Among the options below, which drug can either stimulate or inhibit ovulation, depending solely on how it's scheduled to be taken?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Leuprolide

  • Leuprolide is a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analog. The effect of leuprolide on ovulation depends on the dosing schedule.
  • When administered in a pulsatile fashion, it acts similar to the body's own GnRH, and stimulates the pituitary gland to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which can stimulate ovulation. This effect can be useful in certain fertility treatments.
  • However, when given in a continuous form, leuprolide suppresses the pituitary gland's production of LH and FSH, effectively inhibiting ovulation. This is due to downregulation and desensitization of the GnRH receptors on the pituitary gland.
  • The other drugs listed - Letrozole, Clomiphene, and hCG - have different mechanisms and are not known to both stimulate and inhibit ovulation depending on the dosing schedule. Letrozole and Clomiphene are primarily used to stimulate ovulation, and hCG is used to trigger ovulation in controlled ovarian hyperstimulation cycles.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old individual named Suresh, who has been diagnosed with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, has been prescribed insulin therapy. The discomfort from the injections has become unbearable for him, leading him to attempt consuming the insulin orally from the vial that was initially intended for subcutaneous injection. What is the most likely consequence of his action?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Chronic high blood sugar levels

  • Insulin is a hormone that helps regulate blood glucose levels. It is typically administered through injection because it is a peptide and would be broken down in the digestive system if taken orally, rendering it ineffective. So, if Suresh drinks his insulin instead of injecting it, it will not have the intended effect of lowering his blood glucose levels. This will result in persistent hyperglycemia (high blood sugar levels), which can lead to a variety of health problems if left untreated, including damage to the eyes, kidneys, and nerves, heart disease, stroke, and even diabetic coma.
  • As for the other options, while gastrointestinal upset (A), vomiting (B), and kidney failure (D) can occur in diabetes, they are not the direct result of drinking insulin. These conditions can be related to complications from uncontrolled diabetes or its treatment, but they are not the immediate result of the route of administration of insulin being changed from injection to oral consumption.

questions.stem: Anil, a 63-year-old male with diabetes, currently on sitagliptin, presents to OPD of GTB hospital with complaints of recurring instances of sinusitis and a sore throat. His fasting blood glucose level is 96 mg/dL. What is the most plausible explanation for these symptoms?

options.label: C
options.text: Side effect related to his medication

questions.answerText: Side effect related to his medication
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Side effect related to his medication

  • Sitagliptin is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor used to control blood sugar levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes. One of the common side effects associated with sitagliptin is an upper respiratory tract infection, which could cause symptoms such as a sore throat and sinusitis. Given this, it's most likely that these symptoms are a side effect of her medication.
  • While the other potential causes listed, such as hypersensitivity to environmental allergens (A), acid reflux (B), or a nasal polyp (D), could potentially lead to similar symptoms, they are less likely given the patient's medication use and the recurrent nature of symptoms.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman, diagnosed with osteoporosis, is visiting her doctor for a standard check-up. She is currently taking risedronate. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?

options.label: B
options.text: Inhibition of enzymes involved in mevalonate pathway of cholesterol biosynthesis

questions.answerText: Inhibition of enzymes involved in mevalonate pathway of cholesterol biosynthesis
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Inhibition of enzymes involved in mevalonate pathway of cholesterol biosynthesis

  • Risedronate is a type of medication known as a bisphosphonate, which is commonly used in the treatment of osteoporosis. Bisphosphonates, including risedronate, work primarily by inhibiting farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase (FPPS), an enzyme involved in the mevalonate pathway of cholesterol biosynthesis.
  • FPPS catalyzes the synthesis of farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP), a key intermediate in cholesterol and other sterols. When FPPS is inhibited by risedronate, it disrupts the synthesis of isoprenoid lipids that are crucial for the post-translational modification (prenylation) of small GTPase signaling proteins within the osteoclast. The disruption of these proteins impairs the osteoclast's ability to resorb bone and triggers apoptosis, or programmed cell death, in the osteoclast. This leads to decreased bone resorption and, therefore, to increased bone density, which is beneficial in osteoporosis.

  • The end result is increased apoptosis of osteoclasts, option D is phrased in the opposite way and is therefore incorrect.
  • Option A (Inhibition of osteocyte activation) and option C (Stimulation of osteoblasts) are not the primary mechanisms of action of risedronate.

questions.stem: Considering the standard roles of triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) in a young female presenting with hypothyroidism, which of the following assertions is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The absorption of T3 is reduced by food consumption

options.label: B
options.text: The hormones are broken down through the microsomal P450 system

options.label: C
options.text: Phenytoin slows down the metabolism of thyroid hormones

options.label: D
options.text: Rifampin slows down the metabolism of thyroid hormones

questions.answerText: The hormones are broken down through the microsomal P450 system
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. The hormones are broken down through the microsomal P450 system

  • Triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) are the main hormones produced by the thyroid gland. These hormones are metabolized in the liver, kidneys, brain, and other tissues primarily through reactions catalyzed by enzymes of the cytochrome P450 system.
  • Food intake decreases the absorption of T4 and not T3.
  • Phenytoin and rifampicin are microsomal enzyme inducers. These are known to increase the metabolism of thyroid hormones, not slow it down.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old boy sustains a shoulder injury in a road side accident. Despite using the NSAIDs, he's still struggling with pain and swelling. When he enquires about glucocorticoid injections, his doctor begins discussing the wide range of glucocorticoid effects on the body. In what ways could glucocorticoids potentially assist this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Reducing the activity of phospholipase A2

options.label: B
options.text: Enhancing healing through increased collagen production

questions.answerText: Reducing the activity of phospholipase A2
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Reducing the activity of phospholipase A2

  • Glucocorticoids exert a variety of anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. They inhibit the phospholipase A2 enzyme, which in turn decreases the production of pro-inflammatory eicosanoids such as prostaglandins and leukotrienes. This reduction can help decrease pain and swelling, which is why glucocorticoids may be beneficial in managing the patient's symptoms.
  • Option B is not correct because glucocorticoids actually slow wound healing and reduce collagen formation. They inhibit fibroblast function and thus, they impair the production and organization of key components of the extracellular matrix, such as collagen.
  • Option C is also incorrect. Glucocorticoids do not increase blood flow via vasodilation. In fact, they can cause vasoconstriction in some cases.

So, in the given options, the most accurate one is option A, which refers to the inhibition of phospholipase A2.

questions.stem: Raju, a 50-year-old male is experiencing rapid heart rate, intolerance to heat, tremors, and unexpected weight loss. Her thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels are significantly elevated. He was prescribed a medication to block the release of TSH. Which medication is this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Octreotide

  • The patient's symptoms of tachycardia, heat intolerance, tremor, and unintentional weight loss suggest hyperthyroidism. However, in typical hyperthyroidism, TSH levels would be low, not high, due to negative feedback inhibition on the pituitary gland. This patient's elevated TSH level suggests TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma, which is a rare cause of hyperthyroidism.
  • Octreotide, a somatostatin analogue, can be used to treat this condition. Somatostatin, secreted by the hypothalamus, inhibits the release of many hormones, including growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and various gastrointestinal hormones. Octreotide, being a somatostatin analogue, can reduce the secretion of TSH, thus alleviating the symptoms of hyperthyroidism in this patient.
  • Levothyroxine is used to treat hypothyroidism, not hyperthyroidism.
  • Methimazole and propylthiouracil are used to treat hyperthyroidism, but they work by inhibiting thyroid hormone synthesis in the thyroid gland, not by reducing TSH release.

questions.stem: Metformin is least likely to reduce blood sugar in which of the following patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
g>Explanation of Other Options

A. Obese diabetics

Metformin is particularly effective in obese diabetics because it helps reduce insulin resistance and can aid in weight management, both of which are beneficial in managing type 2 diabetes.

C. Type 2 diabetics

Metformin is a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes and is effective in reducing blood sugar levels in these patients by addressing the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms of the disease.

D. Diabetics not responding to sulfonylureas

Metformin can be effective in diabetics who do not respond to sulfonylureas. It works through different mechanisms, so it can be beneficial as monotherapy or in combination with other antidiabetic medications, including when sulfonylureas alone are insufficient.

Educational Objective

Metformin is a widely used antihyperglycemic agent for managing type 2 diabetes, particularly effective in patients with insulin resistance, such as obese diabetics. It works by decreasing hepatic glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity. However, in non-diabetic individuals, metformin is least likely to reduce blood sugar levels significantly, as their glucose metabolism is generally normal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an indication of oxytocin?
questions.solutionHtml:
yperprolactinemia is typically managed with dopamine agonists such as bromocriptine or cabergoline, which reduce prolactin secretion.

Explanation of Other Options

A. Treatment of breast engorgement

While oxytocin can help with milk ejection by stimulating the contraction of myoepithelial cells around the mammary glands, it is not typically used for the treatment of breast engorgement. Other measures such as manual expression, breastfeeding, or cold compresses are usually recommended for breast engorgement.

B. Induction of labour

Oxytocin is commonly used to induce or augment labor by stimulating uterine contractions. It is a well-established indication for oxytocin use.

C. Postpartum hemorrhage

Oxytocin is also used to manage postpartum hemorrhage by promoting uterine contractions, which help to compress blood vessels and reduce bleeding.

Educational Objective

Oxytocin is primarily used for the induction or augmentation of labor and the management of postpartum hemorrhage due to its ability to stimulate uterine contractions. It is not indicated for the treatment of hyperprolactinemia, which is managed with dopamine agonists.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old postmenopausal woman presents to your clinic with persistent lower back pain for the last three months. She reports the pain is gradually increasing in intensity. The pain is non-radiating and does not change with position or activity. She denies trauma or any other symptoms. Her medical history is notable for hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Her only medications are lisinopril and metformin. Her BMI is 28. A dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan reveals a T-score of -2.7 at the lumbar spine. Laboratory tests show normal calcium, phosphate, and vitamin D levels. You start her treatment with the drug of choice for this condition. Which of the following is the most likely side effect of this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Osteonecrosis of the jaw

The patient's DEXA scan results indicate that she has osteoporosis, which is likely contributing to her persistent back pain. Bisphosphonates, such as alendronate, are commonly used first-line medications for the treatment of osteoporosis. They work by inhibiting osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, thus improving bone density. One of the rare but significant adverse effects of bisphosphonate therapy is osteonecrosis of the jaw, often triggered by dental surgery or tooth extraction.

Other side effects include esophagitis (if not taken properly), hypocalcemia, and atypical femoral fractures with long-term use.

questions.stem: Which of the following drug can decrease bone resorption as well as increase bone formation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Explanation of Other Options

 

A. Denosumab

 

Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits RANKL (receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-Β ligand), leading to decreased bone resorption. It does not significantly increase bone formation. Denosumab is used primarily to prevent bone loss in conditions like osteoporosis and certain cancers.

 

C. Teriparatide

 

Teriparatide is a recombinant form of parathyroid hormone (PTH) that primarily stimulates bone formation. It is used to treat osteoporosis by increasing bone formation but does not significantly decrease bone resorption. Teriparatide is typically reserved for patients with severe osteoporosis or those who have not responded to other treatments.

 

D. Cinacalcet

 

Cinacalcet is a calcimimetic agent used to treat secondary hyperparathyroidism in patients with chronic kidney disease and hypercalcemia in patients with parathyroid carcinoma. It lowers parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels by increasing the sensitivity of calcium-sensing receptors in the parathyroid gland. Cinacalcet does not directly affect bone resorption or formation.

 

Educational Objective

 

Romosozumab uniquely decreases bone resorption and increases bone formation by inhibiting sclerostin. In contrast, denosumab decreases bone resorption by inhibiting RANKL, teriparatide increases bone formation as a recombinant PTH, and cinacalcet lowers PTH levels without directly affecting bone metabolism.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman, Seema was a resident of Nubra Valley in Leh Ladakh. She underwent a kidney transplant at AIIMS, Delhi. After transplant she was started several immunosuppressant drugs, including daily prednisone. She had returned to her home at Nubra Valley and is taking prednisone for the past two months since her transplant. However, she is trapped in her house due to heavy snow and may soon run out of prednisone. What health risk is she most likely to face if she does not get her prednisone in time?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Cardiovascular collapse

  • If a patient suddenly stops taking prednisone after being on it for more than a few weeks, they may not have enough cortisol in their system to respond to stress. This can lead to a serious condition called HPA axis suppression resulting in adrenal crisis or acute adrenal insufficiency, which can manifest as severe fatigue, weakness, nausea, vomiting, low blood pressure, and potentially cardiovascular collapse if not treated. This is why it's important to gradually taper the dose of prednisone, rather than stopping it abruptly.
  • While long-term use of corticosteroids can increase the risk of osteoporosis (option A) and cause sleep disturbances (option D), these are not the immediate risks of abruptly stopping prednisone. These are rather potential long-term side effects of the medication.
  • Increased risk of infections (option B) occurs due to overuse of steroids and is not a complication of sudden stoppage of steroids.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old sexually active female approaches her family doctor seeking a contraceptive. She is a chronic smoker consuming around a pack of cigarettes daily. She also consumes few alcoholic drinks per week. She has no personal or family history of breast, ovarian, or endometrial cancer. What could be the reason for her physician to advise against using a contraceptive containing estrogen?

options.label: B
options.text: The potential for estrogen to disrupt the patient's lipid profile like increasing LDL cholesterol, leading to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease

options.label: C
options.text: High risk of developing endometrial cancer

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Increased risk of thromboembolism

  • This patient is a smoker who is over 35 years old, which significantly increases her risk of thromboembolism if she were to take an estrogen-containing contraceptive. Combined hormonal contraceptives increase the risk of venous thromboembolism because estrogen increases the production of clotting factors. The risk is even higher in women over 35 years old who smoke due to the combined effects of nicotine on the vascular system and the thrombotic effects of estrogen.
  • Option A is not relevant as disulfiram-like reactions are associated with certain medications (like metronidazole and some cephalosporins) and alcohol, not with estrogen.
  • Option B is wrong because estrogen improve lipid profile (decrease LDL/HDL cholesterol ratio).
  • Option C is not the primary concern either, as the patient has no personal or family history of hormone-sensitive cancers. Further combined OCP actually decrease the risk of ovarian cancer.

B: BP ≥ 160/100 mm Hg

S:    Surgery with prolonged immobilization

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with a medical history of diabetes, hypertension, rheumatoid arthritis and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) has been feeling tired for the past 2 weeks. Her current medication regimen includes glipizide, prednisone, telmisartan, and pantoprazole. Her complete blood count shows an elevated white blood cell count with predominant neutrophilia. Which of her medications could potentially be the reason for her increased TLC and neutrophilia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Prednisone

  • Prednisone is a glucocorticoid medication that can lead to an increase in the white blood cell (WBC) count.
  • Glucocorticoids cause demargination of neutrophils, releasing them from the walls of blood vessels and into the circulation, leading to an increase in the count of circulating neutrophils. This is why patients taking prednisone or other glucocorticoid medications may have a higher WBC count.
  • It should be noted that while the total WBC count increases, this does not indicate an infection or an increase in the body's immune response capacity, as glucocorticoids also have immunosuppressive effects.
  • The other medications listed do not cause an elevation in WBC count.

questions.stem: A young couple is having trouble conceiving after nine months of unprotected intercourse. The wife's levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) are normal, and her pelvic exam shows no abnormalities. They agree to a trial of letrozole in hopes of increasing their chances of conception. How does letrozole work?

options.label: C
options.text: It blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. It inhibits aromatase

  • Letrozole is an aromatase inhibitor. Aromatase is an enzyme that is involved in the conversion of androgens to estrogens. By inhibiting this enzyme, letrozole decreases the levels of estrogen in the body. This reduction in estrogen levels leads to an increase in the production of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) by the hypothalamus, and subsequently an increase in follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) release from the pituitary gland. These hormones stimulate the ovulation and thereby increasing the chances of conception.
  • Letrozole does not act on the hypothalamus, increase sperm production, or suppress prolactin secretion.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about dapagliflozin is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Its major mode of action in diabetes mellitus is to cause glucosuria when serum glucose is above 180 mg/dL.

options.label: B
options.text: It acts by inhibiting SGLT2 present in collecting tubules of the nephron

options.label: C
options.text: Urinary tract infections are common with its use

questions.answerText: Urinary tract infections are common with its use
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Urinary tract infections are common with its use

 

Let us analyse each option one by one:

 

Option A. Its major mode of action in diabetes mellitus is to cause glucosuria when serum glucose is above 180 mg/dL: This statement is not correct. Dapagliflozin, an SGLT2 inhibitor, reduces blood glucose levels by blocking glucose reabsorption in the kidneys, leading to increased glucose excretion in the urine (glucosuria). This effect occurs regardless of whether the blood glucose level is above or below 180 mg/dL. The traditional concept of a renal threshold for glucose around 180 mg/dL applies to normal physiology without SGLT2 inhibition. SGLT2 inhibitors lower this threshold, causing glucosuria even at lower blood glucose levels.

 

Option B. It acts by inhibiting SGLT2 present in the collecting tubules of the nephron: This statement is incorrect. Though dapagliflozin inhibits SGLT2 but it is primarily located in the proximal convoluted tubule, not in the collecting tubules.

 

Option C. Urinary tract infections are common with its use: This is true. The use of SGLT2 inhibitors like dapagliflozin is associated with an increased risk of urinary tract infections due to the presence of higher glucose levels in the urine, which can foster bacterial growth.

 

Given this information, the true statement about dapagliflozin is option c: "Urinary tract infections are common with its use."

questions.solutionHtml:

Explanation of Other Options

B. Raloxifene

Raloxifene is a Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM). It acts as an estrogen receptor agonist on bone and lipid metabolism but as an antagonist on breast and uterine tissues. It is used primarily for the prevention and treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and for reducing the risk of invasive breast cancer.

C. Mifepristone

Mifepristone is a progesterone receptor antagonist and a glucocorticoid receptor antagonist. It is used for medical termination of intrauterine pregnancy and for the management of hyperglycemia in patients with Cushing's syndrome. It does not act as a Selective Estrogen Receptor Downregulator.

D. All of these

This option is incorrect because neither raloxifene nor mifepristone act as Selective Estrogen Receptor Downregulators. Only fulvestrant fits this category.

Educational Objective

Selective Estrogen Receptor Downregulators (SERDs) like fulvestrant are used in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer by promoting the degradation of estrogen receptors and reducing estrogen-mediated signaling. Raloxifene, a Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM), and mifepristone, a progesterone receptor antagonist, have different mechanisms of action and therapeutic uses.
